details.description: FLUX.1 [schnell] is a 12 billion parameter rectified flow transformer from Black Forest Labs that generates images from text descriptions. It is trained with latent adversarial diffusion distillation so it "can generate high-quality images in only 1 to 4 steps," and is released under the Apache 2.0 license for personal, scientific, and commercial use. Fireworks AI hosts it (accounts/fireworks/models/flux-1-schnell) for on-demand, dedicated-GPU deployment. As of September 2026, Black Forest Labs' current models page and docs are centered on the newer FLUX.2 and FLUX 3 families and no longer list FLUX.1 [schnell], though the Hugging Face model card remains published with no deprecation notice.
advantages: Trained with latent adversarial diffusion distillation, letting it "generate high-quality images in only 1 to 4 steps" per the model card, far fewer than typical diffusion models.
Released under the Apache 2.0 license, permitting personal, scientific, and commercial use without the restrictions of the FLUX.1 [dev] non-commercial license.
Black Forest Labs describes its output as "cutting-edge output quality and competitive prompt following, matching the performance of closed source alternatives".
disadvantages: The model card states it is not designed for factual information generation.
The model card notes it may amplify existing societal biases.
The model card notes prompt-following performance varies depending on prompt style.
Fireworks lists fine-tuning, serverless deployment, function calling, embeddings, reranking, and image input as not supported for this model.
Does not appear on Black Forest Labs' current models listing, which as of September 2026 is centered on the newer FLUX.2 and FLUX 3 generations.
use_cases: Fast text-to-image generation where low step count/latency matters
Commercial and personal image-generation applications under the Apache 2.0 license

notes: GROUPING/kind conflict: the catalog lists this entry as kind "chat" with endpoint /v1/chat/completions and modality [text_input, text_output], max_input/output_tokens 4096. The maker (Hugging Face card) and host (Fireworks model page, created 2024-10-22 per that page) both confirm this is a text-to-image diffusion model, not a chat/text model, and Fireworks' own fp8 variant of this model (flux-1-schnell-fp8) uses /v1/images/generations with image_output modality instead. Catalog facts were kept as authoritative per instructions; this is flagged as a likely data/routing mismatch rather than restated as a chat capability. No specific benchmark scores were found stated by Black Forest Labs on the pages opened, so evaluations is empty. Superseded status is inferred from BFL's current bfl.ai/models and docs.bfl.ai pages not listing FLUX.1 [schnell] at all (lineup now leads with FLUX.2/FLUX 3); no explicit deprecation notice was found on the Hugging Face card itself.
